newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAD studies penicillin joint venture.
newsitem.headline: SAD studies penicillin joint venture.

text.p: South African Druggist Ltd's Pharmacare unit is to enter a joint study with Indian drug firm Kopran Ltd into setting up a facility to manufacture penicillin-based products in South Africa.
Pharmacare said in a statement the multi-million U.S. dollar project, if approved, would be two-phased and remained dependent on the outcome of the feasibility study.

Phase one will set up the infrastructure required to handle capacities of around 300 to 350 tonnes a year for the manufacture of semi-synthetic penicillins such as ampicillin, amoxycillin and cloxacillin bulk drugs, the company said.
Both partners are intended to have an equal stake in the project.

"Phase two of the project will be to forward integrate into the manufacture of finished dosage forms such as dry syrups, capsules and tablets of penicillin-based products for the local and international markets," Pharmacare added.

Pharmacare chief executive Kobus Nel said the move would be a major breakthrough for drug development in South Africa, entrenching the company's position as a leading manufacturer and supplier of medicines in South Africa and overseas.
The joint venture will establish Pharmacare as the only manufacturer of bulk semi-synthetic penicillins in Southern Africa.
Semi-synthetic penicillins are general anti-biotics used to fight a range of infections from lung diseases to acute typhoid fever.
Kopran Limited is one of the world's largest manufacturer of semi-synthetic penicillins as well as more modern anti-biotic and anti-microbial drugs.
